name: Obsidian
author: E. T. Carter
description: A freshly broken face of black volcanic glass. Shell-shaped fracture scars overlap as layered planes, each fanning out from its own point of percussion and carrying concentric curved ripple ribs and fine radial hackle. The glass reflects a dim tinted studio through a Fresnel skin, tight speculars spark on the rib crests, razor flake edges glint as bright hairlines, and smoky flow bands sit frozen inside the black as the lights slowly circle.

params.label: Fracture scale
params.effect: Size of the fracture shells against the frame; low is a wide face with many small scars, high is a close-up of one or two big shells.

params.label: Rib height
params.effect: Height of the conchoidal ripple ribs and hackle; 0 is smooth polished planes, high is a deeply rippled break.

params.label: Light drift
params.effect: How fast the key light and the reflected strip lights circle the stone; 0 holds them still.

params.label: Polish
params.effect: Strength of the reflections, speculars and edge glints; low is a dull weathered face, high is wet glass.

params.label: Palette tint
params.effect: How much palette colour enters the reflected studio and the smoke inside the glass; 0 is pure silver-on-black.

params.label: Mouse influence
params.effect: How far the pointer pulls the soft-box across the glass; 0 ignores the mouse.
